authors: Stack, Williams, Calef and the Mars 2020 Science Team (2020)
epochNote: Pre-landing photogeologic interpretations. These hypotheses are not mineral assays or updated rover-confirmed rock origins.

units.name: Crater rim rough
units.label: Rough crater rim
units.description: Pitted, light-toned rough terrain with dark sand in small depressions.
units.observations: Coarse layering near edges; numerous retained craters.
units.interpretation: Sedimentary or explosive volcanic deposition was proposed.

units.name: Crater rim layered
units.label: Layered crater rim
units.description: Light-toned, fractured layers in older rim bedrock.
units.observations: Layers from less than a metre to metre scale; local folds and faults.
units.interpretation: Pre-impact basement, possibly sedimentary or explosive volcanic.

units.name: Nili Planum fractured
units.label: Fractured Nili Planum
units.description: Fractured, blocky outcrops outside the crater.
units.interpretation: Several volcanic, impact and sedimentary origins remained possible.

units.name: Crater rim blocky
units.label: Blocky crater rim
units.description: Resistant, rubbly ridges in the crater rim.
units.observations: Boulder-producing relief without obvious internal layering.
units.interpretation: Older bedrock uplifted by the Jezero impact.

units.name: Crater rim breccia
units.label: Crater-rim breccia
units.observations: Blocks tens to more than one hundred metres wide; occasional faint bedding.
units.interpretation: Impact breccia; its association with Jezero or older Isidis events is uncertain.

units.name: Neretva Vallis layered
units.label: Neretva channel layers
units.description: Layered outcrops in the ancient inlet valley.
units.observations: Narrow cracks and reticulate fracture patterns.
units.interpretation: Possibly lithified river deposits related to channel incision.

units.name: Delta blocky
units.label: Blocky delta deposits
units.description: Boulder-shedding mesas, ridges and terraces in the delta.
units.observations: Varied tones and blocks on steep-sided positive relief.

units.name: Delta thinly layered
units.label: Thin delta layers
units.description: Fine, alternating light and dark layers.
units.observations: Beds thinner than a metre, locally folded or polygonally fractured.
units.interpretation: Fine lake, prodelta, floodplain or alluvial sediment was proposed.

units.name: Delta thickly layered
units.label: Thick delta layers
units.description: Resistant delta layers that can be traced over long distances.
units.observations: Rough layers several metres thick, extending hundreds of metres.
units.interpretation: Delta-front, channel-lobe, floodplain or alluvial deposits.

units.name: Delta truncated curvilinear layered
units.label: Curving delta layers
units.description: Curved sets of layers that cut across earlier beds.
units.observations: Alternating strata and laterally continuous boundaries.
units.interpretation: Possible meandering-river point bars or underwater channel-levee complexes.

units.name: Delta layered rough
units.label: Rough layered delta
units.description: Rough, parallel layers in a delta remnant.
units.observations: Metre-scale beds traceable for roughly a hundred metres.
units.interpretation: Distal delta deposits; the supplying fan system was uncertain.

units.name: Margin fractured
units.label: Fractured inner margin
units.description: Fractured rocks along the inner crater margin.
units.observations: Polygonal patterns, short ridges and blocky or lower-relief exposures.
units.interpretation: Multiple origins were proposed, including a near-shore carbonate-bearing setting. This map is not a carbonate measurement.

units.name: Crater floor fractured 1
units.label: Lower fractured floor
units.description: Fractured crater-floor bedrock in the lower elevation range.
units.observations: Polygon networks, long ridges and curved furrows; mapped below about −2530 m.
units.interpretation: Ash, wind-deposited or water-laid sediment were among the pre-landing hypotheses.

units.name: Crater floor fractured 2
units.label: Upper fractured floor
units.description: Blocky and pock-marked floor exposures above the lower floor unit.
units.observations: Arcuate and polygonal fractures; mapped at roughly −2530 to −2440 m.
units.interpretation: Volcanic, wind-deposited and water-laid origins were debated before landing.

units.name: Crater floor fractured rough
units.label: Rough fractured floor
units.description: Rough, crater-retaining and boulder-producing floor bedrock.
units.interpretation: Lithified bedrock with volcanic or sedimentary origins proposed before landing.
